name: Huis Bartolotti, Herengracht 170-172

dates.altered: Remodelled 1735 and 1757 (Amsterdam Monumentenstad); restored 1967-71, when the top of the front gable and the corner chimneys were reconstructed (1968/69), again 1995/97, and the interior in 2015.
dates.note: Three dates are in the sources and none is resolved. The Rijksmonumentenregister says 'Huis uit 1622'; Amsterdam Monumentenstad gives 'Bouwjaar: ca. 1618, 1735, 1757'; the Dutch Wikipedia article says 'circa 1617 gebouwd' while its own infobox prints 'Gereed 1622'. The style node's exemplar year is 1617.

quotes.text: Huis uit 1622, waarschijnlijk door Hendrik de Keyser, met pilastergevel. Zeer fraaie Louis XIV stucgang.
quotes.page: Rijksmonumentenregister, monument 1761, section 'Omschrijving'. A register entry is not paginated.

note: Tranche 3, Low Countries cluster, 5 September 2026. THE REGISTER DISAGREES WITH EVERY OTHER SOURCE ABOUT WHAT KIND OF GABLE THIS IS, and the disagreement is left standing rather than resolved: the Rijksmonumentenregister's description says 'met pilastergevel', while Amsterdam Monumentenstad records 'Geveltype: Trapgevel' and the node's own exemplar note calls it 'the fullest surviving Amsterdam Renaissance stepped gable'. Both can be read as true of one wall -- the gable is a stepped top carried on a facade articulated with pilasters -- but the register's one-line description names only the pilasters, so a reader taking the register as the authority would not learn that this is a stepped gable at all.
